body:
Connecting international events with geography

International conflicts and territorial disputes frequently involve borders, coastal regions, islands, rivers and mountain barriers. Understanding the permanent geographical setting of a conflict is distinct from memorising temporary military or political developments.

Political control and internationally recognised sovereignty are not always identical. A region's geographical location remains relevant even when its political status is disputed or its administration changes.

Eastern Europe and the Black Sea region

Ukraine lies in eastern Europe, with Russia to its east and the Black Sea to its south. The Crimean Peninsula projects into the Black Sea and is separated from the Taman Peninsula by the Kerch Strait.

Crimea is internationally recognised as part of Ukraine, while Russia claims sovereignty over it. These positions must not be treated as an undisputed territorial settlement.

PlaceGeographical identity
DonbasEastern Ukrainian region associated principally with Donetsk and Luhansk
CrimeaPeninsula in the northern Black Sea
OdesaUkrainian city on the Black Sea coast
DnieperMajor river flowing through Ukraine towards the Black Sea
Kerch StraitPassage between the Black Sea and Sea of Azov

The eastern Mediterranean and western Asia

Western Asia lies at the meeting point of Asia, Europe and Africa. The Mediterranean, Red Sea, Persian Gulf and Caspian Sea provide important reference points for locating its countries.

Region or placeGeographical location
Gaza StripMediterranean coast, bordering Israel and Egypt
West BankWest of the Jordan River, adjoining Israel and Jordan
RafahSouthern Gaza near the Egyptian border
Golan HeightsElevated region adjoining southwestern Syria and Israel
LebanonEastern Mediterranean coast, north of Israel
YemenSouthern Arabian Peninsula
Sinai PeninsulaEgypt, between the gulfs of Suez and Aqaba
Kurdish-inhabited regionsParts of Türkiye, Syria, Iraq and Iran

The Gaza Strip has a Mediterranean coastline, while the West Bank is inland. The West Bank's name refers to its location on the western side of the Jordan River.

Yemen lies at the southern entrance to the Red Sea region, near Bab el-Mandeb. It does not border the Persian Gulf.

The Caucasus and Central Asia

The Caucasus region lies between the Black Sea and Caspian Sea. Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan are its principal South Caucasus countries.

Georgia has a Black Sea coastline, Azerbaijan has a Caspian Sea coastline and Armenia is landlocked.

Nagorno-Karabakh is a region within the internationally recognised territory of Azerbaijan. Its geographical and historical association with Armenia has made it central to disputes between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

Afghanistan lies between Central Asia and South Asia. It is landlocked and contains extensive mountain systems, including the Hindu Kush.

Conflict-related regions of Africa

RegionGeographical identity
DarfurWestern Sudan, near Chad
KordofanCentral and south-central Sudan
SahelSemi-arid belt south of the Sahara
Horn of AfricaBroadly Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti
SomalilandNorthwestern part of Somalia, along the Gulf of Aden
Eastern Democratic Republic of the CongoCentral African region near Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi
Lake Chad regionBorder region involving Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon

Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger are important landlocked countries within the wider Sahel region. The Sahel is a geographical belt rather than a single country.

The Horn of Africa projects towards the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea region. Ethiopia is landlocked, whereas Somalia, Eritrea and Djibouti have coastlines.

Eastern and southeastern Asia

Region or placeGeographical location
TaiwanIsland east of mainland China, across the Taiwan Strait
Spratly IslandsSouthern South China Sea
Paracel IslandsNorthern South China Sea, southeast of Hainan
Senkaku or Diaoyu IslandsEast China Sea
Korean PeninsulaBetween the Yellow Sea and Sea of Japan
Rakhine StateWestern Myanmar along the Bay of Bengal
Cox's BazarSoutheastern Bangladesh near Myanmar

The Spratly and Paracel islands are associated with overlapping territorial claims in the South China Sea. The Senkaku or Diaoyu Islands are associated with a separate dispute in the East China Sea.

Rakhine State and Cox's Bazar are geographically connected through the Myanmar-Bangladesh border region and the northeastern Bay of Bengal.

Prelims focus

  • Crimea lies in the Black Sea region.
  • Gaza has a Mediterranean coastline; the West Bank is inland.
  • Armenia is landlocked, while Georgia borders the Black Sea.
  • Darfur is in western Sudan.
  • Rakhine State is in western Myanmar.
  • Trap: Spratly Islands lie in the South China Sea; Senkaku or Diaoyu Islands lie in the East China Sea.

[References: United Nations Geospatial, Map of the World, July 2026 revision; United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, Security Council briefing on Ukraine, 23 November 2026; United Nations Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Report to the Ad Hoc Liaison Committee, September 2026; United Nations in Sudan, Severe Rainfall Deficits in Sudan, 16 October 2026; UNHCR statement on The Gambia v. Myanmar judgment, 19 November 2026; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

title: Conflict Regions and Their Geographical Setting

body:
Separating permanent geography from changing events

A location may become important because of an international conflict, environmental development, trade disruption, natural disaster or international designation. Its permanent geographical characteristics include its country, continent, neighbouring regions and surrounding water bodies.

Current-affairs information must be associated with its reporting period. A report describing an event in a particular month does not necessarily describe conditions on every subsequent date.

The current-affairs examples below use a content cutoff of 26 November 2026. Dated developments are identified by their reporting or designation dates rather than presented as permanent facts.

The Black Sea and international food trade

The Black Sea provides maritime access for several eastern European and western Asian countries. Its connection to the Mediterranean through the Turkish Straits gives it importance in international agricultural trade.

In a United Nations Security Council briefing on 23 November 2026, the UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs reported continuing disruption to civilian shipping and food exports in the Black Sea during the ongoing conflict involving Russia and Ukraine.

The geographical distinction to retain is that the Black Sea reaches the Mediterranean through the Bosporus, Sea of Marmara, Dardanelles and Aegean Sea. It does not connect directly to the Atlantic Ocean.

Western Asian maritime trade in 2026

The Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Arabian Sea and Red Sea are important geographical components of international energy trade.

A US Energy Information Administration analysis published on 19 November 2026 reported that combined oil shipments through Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal-SUMED system increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the second quarter. The report also indicated that individual waterways experienced different trends during that period.

The enduring geographical facts are the connections of the waterways: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman; Bab el-Mandeb links the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden; and Suez connects the Red Sea and Mediterranean Sea.

Gaza and the eastern Mediterranean

The Gaza Strip occupies a small coastal area along the eastern Mediterranean Sea. Humanitarian developments frequently bring Gaza, Rafah and the neighbouring Sinai Peninsula into international news.

A joint statement from the International Organization for Migration and World Food Programme dated 17 November 2026 warned of continuing humanitarian difficulties in Gaza during the approach of winter. This describes the humanitarian situation reported at that time rather than a permanent geographical condition.

Sudan, Darfur and the Sahel

Sudan lies in northeastern Africa and has a coastline on the Red Sea. Its western region, Darfur, adjoins Chad and lies partly within the wider Sahel-Saharan transition.

On 16 October 2026, the United Nations in Sudan reported that rainfall deficits were worsening humanitarian conditions, particularly in Darfur and parts of Kordofan, where the effects of prolonged conflict were already severe.

Darfur belongs to Sudan, not South Sudan. Chad lies to Sudan's west, while South Sudan lies to its south.

Myanmar and the Bay of Bengal

Myanmar occupies the eastern side of the Bay of Bengal and has an extensive coastline extending towards the Andaman Sea. Rakhine State lies along western Myanmar.

On 19 November 2026, UNHCR issued a statement following the International Court of Justice judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar, referring to the continuing displacement of Rohingya communities in Myanmar and neighbouring countries.

The relevant geographical relationship is between Rakhine State in Myanmar, the southeastern coastal region of Bangladesh and the Bay of Bengal.

Recent international geographical designations

Places in international news are not restricted to conflict regions. Mountains, volcanoes, national parks and geological sites can also become important through international recognition.

UNESCO recognised Tungurahua Volcano and Napo Sumaco as new UNESCO Global Geoparks on 10 April 2025. Both are in Ecuador, South America, and remained listed in UNESCO's geographical directory at the content cutoff.

Tungurahua is an active volcano in the Ecuadorian Andes. Its identification connects 3 geographical facts: Ecuador is in western South America, the Andes extend along the continent's western side and the region is associated with Pacific-margin tectonic activity.

PlaceCountryGeographical association
TungurahuaEcuadorAndes Mountains
Napo SumacoEcuadorEastern Andean region
Lang SonVietnamNorthern Vietnam
North RiyadhSaudi ArabiaArabian Peninsula
DanyangSouth KoreaKorean Peninsula

All 5 sites in the table received UNESCO Global Geopark designation in 2025.

Integrated geographical associations

Several geographical features are best remembered together because they belong to the same physical region.

RegionAssociated features
Western South AmericaAndes, Atacama Desert, Humboldt Current
Southwestern AfricaNamib Desert, Benguela Current, Atlantic Ocean
Northeastern AfricaNile, Red Sea, Ethiopian Highlands
Northern AsiaSiberia, Ob, Yenisei, Lena, Arctic Ocean
Eastern North AmericaAppalachians, Gulf Stream, Labrador Current region
Western North AmericaRockies, California Current, Colorado River
Southern AsiaHimalayas, Indus, Ganga-Brahmaputra, Indian Ocean
Southeastern AsiaMekong, South China Sea, Strait of Malacca
Central AsiaAral Sea, Amu Darya, Syr Darya, Tian Shan
Eastern MediterraneanGaza, Lebanon, Suez Canal region

Geographical reasoning through location and connection

A feature can often be identified by examining its relationships with better-known geographical features. For example, the combination of a cold ocean current, a coastal desert and a long mountain system along western South America identifies the Humboldt Current, Atacama Desert and Andes region.

Similarly, the combination of an inland sea, Europe's longest river and the eastern side of the Caucasus identifies the Caspian Sea region and the Volga River.

Understanding these relationships is more reliable than remembering isolated names. It also helps distinguish locations that belong to the same continent but have different geographical characteristics.

Prelims focus

  • Black Sea connects to the Mediterranean through the Turkish Straits.
  • Darfur belongs to Sudan, not South Sudan.
  • Rakhine State lies along Myanmar's western coast.
  • Tungurahua Volcano is situated in Ecuador in the Andes.
  • The Namib-Benguela and Atacama-Humboldt pairs illustrate related coastal geography.
  • Trap: A temporary political or humanitarian development should not be memorised as an unchanging geographical fact.

[References: United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, Security Council briefing on Ukraine, 23 November 2026; U.S. Energy Information Administration, Oil Flows Through Middle East Chokepoints Increased in the Third Quarter, 19 November 2026, reporting July–September 2026 data; IOM and WFP, Winter Hits Gaza Hard as Food and Shelter Aid Runs Short, joint statement dated 17 November 2026; United Nations in Sudan, Severe Rainfall Deficits in Sudan, 16 October 2026; UNHCR, statement on The Gambia v. Myanmar judgment, 19 November 2026; UNESCO, Ecuador Adds Two New UNESCO Global Geoparks, 19 May 2025, and UNESCO International Geoscience and Geoparks Programme directory; NOAA, JetStream Max: Major Ocean Currents; Orient BlackSwan School Atlas, World – Physical, p. 81; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]
